Ecommerce Concepts

Foundational business domain concepts explained simply for developers building ecommerce applications, integrations, and APIs.

concept beginner

Product Bundles

A product bundle is a collection of multiple distinct items packaged and sold together as a single commercial offering, often at a discounted price.
comparison beginner

3PL vs In-House Fulfillment

Compare outsourced 3PL logistics services against self-managed in-house warehouse fulfillment.
concept beginner

Barcode (UPC / EAN / GTIN)

A barcode is a standardized, machine-readable numerical code assigned globally to identify commercial items across supply chains and retailers.
concept beginner

Third-Party Logistics (3PL)

A 3PL (Third-Party Logistics) provider is an outsourced fulfillment service that handles inventory storage, pick-and-pack, shipping, and returns for merchants.
comparison beginner

Catalog vs Inventory

Understand the fundamental difference between marketing catalog definitions and physical inventory stock tracking.
concept beginner

Catalog

A catalog is the master repository of all products, variants, collections, categories, and media offered by an ecommerce merchant.
concept beginner

Coupon & Promo Code

A coupon code is an alphanumeric string entered by a customer at checkout to redeem a specific promotional discount rule.
concept beginner

Customer

A customer represents an individual or organization purchasing goods or services from an ecommerce store.
concept beginner

Discount

A discount is a price reduction applied automatically or via coupon codes to incentives purchases, boost conversion rates, or clear inventory.
concept beginner

Fulfillment

Fulfillment encompasses the complete operational pipeline of receiving, picking, packing, shipping, and delivering customer orders.
comparison beginner

Discount vs Coupon

Understand the distinction between underlying price reduction rules and customer-facing promo code triggers.
concept beginner

Inventory

Inventory is the physical or digital quantity of sellable product variants available at specified fulfillment locations.
concept beginner

Location

A location represents a physical or logical site where inventory is stocked, fulfilled, or processed.
comparison beginner

Merchant vs Vendor

Understand the commercial relationship between retail merchants and product suppliers/vendors.
concept beginner

Merchant

A merchant is the business entity or seller operating an ecommerce store and selling products directly to buyers.
concept beginner

Order

An order is an immutable financial and fulfillment contract representing a customer's purchase agreement.
comparison beginner

Order vs Transaction

Understand the architectural boundary between merchant purchase contracts and payment gateway transactions.
concept beginner

Payment Gateway

A payment gateway is the software service that securely encrypts, authorizes, and processes credit card or digital wallet transactions between shoppers and merchants.
concept beginner

Product

A product represents a distinct item or service that a merchant offers for sale in an ecommerce store.
comparison beginner

Product vs Variant

Understand the core structural difference between high-level product containers and specific sellable option configurations.
concept beginner

Price & Compare-At Price

Price represents the monetary value required to purchase a variant, while Compare-At Price displays the original reference list price for strike-through sales.
concept beginner

Retailer

A retailer is a commercial business that purchases goods from manufacturers or distributors and sells them directly to end consumers.
concept beginner

SKU (Stock Keeping Unit)

A SKU is a unique alphanumeric identifier assigned internally by a merchant to track a specific product variant and its inventory.
comparison beginner

SKU vs Barcode

Understand the fundamental differences between internal merchant SKUs and globally standardized barcodes (UPC / EAN / GTIN).
concept beginner

Subscription Commerce

Subscription commerce is a business model where customers pay a recurring fee at specified intervals to receive recurring product deliveries or digital access.
concept beginner

Ecommerce Supply Chain

An ecommerce supply chain is the end-to-end network of organizations, resources, activities, and technologies involved in creating and delivering products to shoppers.
comparison beginner

User vs Customer

Clarify the technical boundary between backend admin users and storefront customer accounts.
concept beginner

Variant

A variant is a specific sellable configuration of a product defined by a combination of options such as size, color, or material.
concept beginner

Vendor

A vendor is a brand, manufacturer, or supplier that provides products to a merchant for retail sale.
comparison beginner

Warehouse vs Location

Understand the difference between physical warehouse buildings and platform inventory location abstractions.
concept beginner

Warehouse

A warehouse is a physical industrial facility dedicated to receiving, storing, picking, packing, and dispatching product inventory.
